guarantees.claim: message_length_d is initially set to message_length as a default value.
guarantees.cond: always at the start of the combinational block

guarantees.claim: When hash_start is high, message_length_d is forced to zero, overriding all prior assignments in this block.
When hash_start is low and msg_write, sha_en, and packer_ready are all high, message_length_d is set to message_length + wmask_ones, overriding CSR loads.

When cfg_block is low, hash_start is low, not (msg_write && sha_en && packer_ready), and reg2hw.msg_length_lower.qe is high, the lower 32 bits of message_length_d are loaded from reg2hw.msg_length_lower.q.

When cfg_block is low, hash_start is low, not (msg_write && sha_en && packer_ready), and reg2hw.msg_length_upper.qe is high, the upper 32 bits of message_length_d are loaded from reg2hw.msg_length_upper.q.

assumptions.claim: wmask_ones precisely reflects the number of valid bytes in the current write operation.
assumptions.cond: when msg_write, sha_en, and packer_ready are all high
assumptions.risk: If wmask_ones is incorrect, message_length will be corrupted, leading to HMAC tag mismatch or integrity bypass.

assumptions.claim: hash_start is asserted only for a single cycle at the beginning of a new hash operation.
assumptions.cond: when a new message is to be hashed
assumptions.risk: If hash_start remains high for multiple cycles, message_length_d stays zero, preventing length accumulation and potentially breaking the hash protocol.

assumptions.claim: message_length + wmask_ones does not overflow the 64-bit counter.
assumptions.cond: when the increment path is active (hash_start low and handshake asserted)
assumptions.risk: Overflow could cause message length wrap-around, leading to incorrect final padding and HMAC forgery.

uncertain_points.claim: The exact compile-time generate conditions that enable this block are unclear from the guard context; signals like reg2hw.msg_length_lower.qe and hash_start appear as if they could be parameters, potentially causing the block to be absent in configurations where it is needed.
uncertain_points.risk: If the block is omitted due to misconfiguration, message_length_d may be undriven or stuck, causing HMAC length tracking to fail.

uncertain_points.claim: The CSR load path allows software to directly set message_length_d to arbitrary values via reg2hw.msg_length_lower and upper registers, bypassing the normal incremental length tracking.
uncertain_points.cond: when reg2hw.msg_length_lower.qe or .msg_length_upper.qe is high and no hash_start or data write is active
uncertain_points.risk: An adversary or buggy driver could manipulate the message length to produce a valid HMAC for an untrusted message, violating integrity guarantees.

uncertain_points.claim: If hash_start is asserted during the same cycle as a data write handshake (msg_write && sha_en && packer_ready), the length is reset to zero and the increment from the current write is lost.
uncertain_points.cond: hash_start == 1'b1 while msg_write, sha_en, packer_ready are all high
uncertain_points.risk: The message length will be too short, causing HMAC verification failure or possible forgery.
